1	# Creating a command
2	
3	Commands are declared with `defineCommand`, `defineOption` and `defineArgument`, on top of `cliparse`. Options and arguments are validated and parsed by [Zod](https://zod.dev) schemas, and their types flow into the handler. The reasons behind this design are explained in [ADR 0001](../adr/adr-0001-rework-file-structure.md).
4	
5	Before writing a command, look at a similar one and copy its naming, file layout, output format and error messages. `src/commands/drain/` is a good example of a command group with shared arguments and options.
6	
7	## Example
8	
9	A fictional `clever coffee brew <blend>` subcommand, part of a `coffee` group (neither exists in the CLI). The `<blend>` argument is shared by several `coffee` subcommands, so it lives in `coffee.args.js`:
10	
11	```js
12	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.args.js
13	import { z } from 'zod';
14	import { defineArgument } from '../../lib/define-argument.js';
15	
16	export const blendArg = defineArgument({
17	  schema: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, 'Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes'),
18	  description: 'Blend of coffee',
19	  placeholder: 'blend',
20	});
21	```
22	
23	`--shots`, `--milk` and `--topping` are only used by this subcommand, so they are defined inline. `--format` comes from `global.options.js`:
24	
25	```js
26	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.brew.command.js
27	import { z } from 'zod';
28	import { brewCoffee } from '../../clever-client/coffee.js';
29	import { defineCommand } from '../../lib/define-command.js';
30	import { defineOption } from '../../lib/define-option.js';
31	import { Logger } from '../../logger.js';
32	import { sendToApi } from '../../models/send-to-api.js';
33	import { humanJsonOutputFormatOption } from '../global.options.js';
34	import { blendArg } from './coffee.args.js';
35	
36	export const coffeeBrewCommand = defineCommand({
37	  description: 'Brew a coffee',
38	  since: null,
39	  options: {
40	    shots: defineOption({
41	      name: 'shots',
42	      schema: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(1),
43	      description: 'Number of espresso shots',
44	      aliases: ['s'],
45	      placeholder: 'shots',
46	    }),
47	    milk: defineOption({
48	      name: 'milk',
49	      schema: z.enum(['none', 'whole', 'oat']).default('none'),
50	      description: 'Kind of milk',
51	      placeholder: 'milk',
52	    }),
53	    toppings: defineOption({
54	      name: 'topping',
55	      schema: z
56	        .union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])
57	        .transform((value) => (typeof value === 'string' ? [value] : value))
58	        .optional(),
59	      description: 'Topping to add. Multiple --topping can be passed',
60	      placeholder: 'topping',
61	    }),
62	    format: humanJsonOutputFormatOption,
63	  },
64	  args: [blendArg],
65	  async handler(options, blend) {
66	    const { shots, milk, toppings, format } = options;
67

import re,glob
for f in glob.glob('drain.*.command.js')+['drain.command.js']:
    s=open(f).read()
    s=s.replace("import * as Application from '../../models/application.js';\n","")
    s=s.replace("import { formatDrain } from '../../models/drain.js';","import { formatDrain, resolveDrainResource } from '../../models/drain.js';")
    if 'resolveDrainResource' not in s:
        s=s.replace("import { DRAIN_TYPE_CLI_CODES, DRAIN_TYPES } from","import { DRAIN_TYPE_CLI_CODES, DRAIN_TYPES, resolveDrainResource } from")
    if 'resolveDrainResource' not in s:
        s=s.replace("import { sendToApi }","import { resolveDrainResource } from '../../models/drain.js';\nimport { sendToApi }")
    s=re.sub(r"import \{ aliasOption, appIdOrNameOption(, humanJsonOutputFormatOption)? \} from","import { addonIdOrRealIdOption, aliasOption, appIdOrNameOption\\1 } from",s)
    s=s.replace("    app: appIdOrNameOption,\n","    app: appIdOrNameOption,\n    addon: addonIdOrRealIdOption,\n",1)
    s=s.replace("const { alias, app: appIdOrName, format } = options;","const { alias, app: appIdOrName, addon: addonIdOrRealId, format } = options;")
    s=s.replace("const { alias, app: appIdOrName } = options;","const { alias, app: appIdOrName, addon: addonIdOrRealId } = options;")
    s=s.replace("await Application.resolveId(appIdOrName, alias)","await resolveDrainResource(alias, appIdOrName, addonIdOrRealId)")
    s=s.replace("appId: applicationId","resourceId")
    s=s.replace("applicationId","resourceId")
    open(f,'w').write(s)

All six drain commands (`drain`, `create`, `get`, `enable`, `disable`, `remove`) now accept `--addon <addon-id>` (add-on ID or real ID). I didn't run any drain command against the API, so no real add-on has been tried. `npm run fix-all` and `npm run validate` pass, and `clever drain get --help` lists the new option.

- **Resolution:** `src/models/drain.js` already had an unused `resolveDrainResource(alias, app, addon)` helper. I wired the commands to it. It resolves an add-on to its real ID, the same way `clever logs --addon` does.
- **Conflicting options:** combining `--addon` with `--app` or `--alias` is rejected with an error. This is the helper's existing behaviour.
- **Client mismatch:** the commands were passing `applicationId` to `src/clever-client/drains.js`, but those functions read `resourceId`. I switched the commands to `resourceId`.
- **Docs:** regenerated `drain.docs.md` and the skill's `full-documentation.md`.
- **Dependencies:** `node_modules` wasn't installed, so I ran `npm ci` to be able to lint and validate.
- **`.claude/settings.json`:** the formatter rewrote it, and I reverted it since it's unrelated.

Nothing is committed.
